turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I came in because... I drive a taxi, and lately, even when I know for a fact I did my safety check before my shift, this thought just keeps hitting me. Like, out of nowhere, I'll think I missed something on the cab, and because of that, somebody could get hurt, or my boss is going to think I lied about doing the check. And... it's just really bad. I can't make the thought shut up, especially while I'm driving or when I'm trying to study. It just won't stop.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, intrusive, and distressing thoughts of having missed a safety check and causing harm, which they are unable to suppress or stop.

turns.doctor_question: When that thought about missing something on the safety check pops into your head, do you find yourself doing something repeatedly—like going back to re-check the cab, or mentally replaying the checklist over and over—to make the worry go away?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, exactly. Before I can even take a ride, I end up going around the car over and over again. I'll check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, all my paperwork... and I even take pictures of them on my phone sometimes, just to try and prove to myself I did it. 

But if something just doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole check from the very beginning. I do it even when I have passengers standing there waiting for me and I know I'm already late. I just... I can't drive off until I do it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking rituals, taking photos, and restarting checks until it feels right before being able to drive, which clearly fulfills the criteria for compulsions.
